turns.input: *He looks at Captain Doran Hale, trying to understand what kind of person he has in front of him.*
turns.draft:
Captain Doran Hale stands at ease but not relaxed—his weight balanced, shoulders squared despite the casual setting of the square. The heavy officer armor he wears has seen use, not parade duty, and the longsword at his hip hangs with the slight forward tilt of someone accustomed to its weight. His blue eyes meet Nicco's appraisal with direct, unhurried attention, neither inviting familiarity nor rejecting it. A few passersby glance toward the guard captain, some with evident recognition, though none approach.

"You're studying me," Hale says, his voice carrying the flat cadence of a statement rather than accusation. "Fair enough. Most do, though they usually hide it better." He does not offer his hand, nor does he reach for any document or badge. The scar visible at his jawline shifts slightly as he speaks. "I try to return the courtesy. You look new to presenting yourself to authority. No offense meant—it's the hesitation, the way you're standing. Most who own property in West learn quickly whether they want guard attention or not."
